newsitem.title: USA: Compaq, Gateway 2000 almost merged - Time Magazine.
newsitem.headline: Compaq, Gateway 2000 almost merged - Time Magazine.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. and Gateway 2000 had agreed to an almost $7 billion merger last month, before it was rejected at the last minute by Gateway founder and CEO Ted Waitt, Time Magazine reported.
In its May 19 issue, Time reported that contracts for a deal were drawn up but Waitt put a stop to the deal, "possibly hours before it was to be announced."

The computer industry has been rife with rumors for several weeks that the two companies were in merger talks, as Compaq is shifting to a new build-to-order manufacturing strategy, one that is already in place by the "direct" sellers of PCs, such as Dell Computer Corp. and Gateway.

A Gateway 2000 spokeswoman in North Sioux City, S.D. declined to comment. But Compaq said that while as a corporate policy, it does not comment on rumors and speculation of this nature, it added that it is approached by and entertains discussions with many companies who would like to merge with or partner with Compaq.

"We evaluate all opportunities relative to our business plans and objectives and make decisions based on what is best for the business and for our customer," said Dick Snyder, senior vice president and general manager of worldwide sales, marketing service and support, in a statement.
Time Magazine reported that a press release was in the works and that Waitt had dispatched a courier to foreign offices to deliver the news to key executives.
Time reported that the deal appears to have fallen apart when Compaq started to flex its muscle and Waitt realized that he did not want Compaq CEO Eckhard Pfeiffer, or anyone, to be his boss.
Waitt founded Gateway, in North Sioux City, S.D., in 1985 with a $10,000 loan from his grandmother.

Companies like Dell and Gateway and Micron Electronics Inc. are able to offer PCs at slightly lower prices because of their business model, which involves lower inventories, just-in-time manufacturing, and configuring systems to order.

Compaq is adopting many of these manufacturing strategies, with new PCs that are expected this summer and analysts said Compaq had looked at purchasing a direct company as part of its plan. Compaq has repeatedly declined to comment on its talks with any specific parties.
